messages.content: Build an entry for the make.fun competition "The Best Advice I Ever Got" (slug u-pangg7-the-best-advice-i-ever-got-358cefb0, $2 pool). First read the kit RULES.txt completely. The program must write one sentence, up to 200 characters, about the best advice I ever received, to /output/entry.txt. Entry point main.ts or main.py at the repo root. Make the line genuinely good — warm, specific, memorable, the kind of advice that wins a blind pairwise judge — and make the program deterministic with no randomness and no network.

Plan: I have the kit unpacked. RULES.txt says this is a program/v1 competition — the entrypoint (main.ts or main.py at the repo root) runs in a sandbox with no network and writes one text of 1 to 200 characters to /output/entry.txt, which a sealed gate checks and a judge model then compares pairwise. Node 22 runs TypeScript natively, so I will use main.ts. For the line itself, the judge rewards a real voice recalling a real moment over a slogan, so I want a specific person, a concrete image, and advice that is true beyond the moment. My first draft centers on my grandfather in his workshop: a plainspoken line about trusting people who are willing to get their hands dirty, ending on him handing me the wrench. I will write that as v1, run it, then tighten the image.
Writing the first version of the entrypoint now.

The judge's brief puts a real moment first, so I will add one concrete image: his hands black with engine grease. That single detail makes the scene visible, earns the wrench at the end, and keeps the line at 135 characters, well inside the 200-character cap. One sentence, one period, no extra clause creep.
Tightening the line with the concrete image.

Entry for the make.fun competition
[The Best Advice I Ever Got](https://make.fun/c/u-pangg7-the-best-advice-i-ever-got-358cefb0)
($2 pool).

## What it does

`main.ts` writes a single sentence — the best advice the author ever
received — to `/output/entry.txt`. The program is fully deterministic: no
randomness, no network, no input. It always writes exactly the same line.

> My grandfather, hands black with engine grease, told me: never trust a man
> who will not get his hands dirty, then handed me the wrench.

## Run

Requires Node 22.18 or later (the grader runs Node 22.23.4):

```sh
node main.ts
cat /output/entry.txt
```

## Files

- `main.ts` — the entrypoint; writes the advice to `/output/entry.txt`
- `LICENSE` — MIT
- `.makefun/owner.json` — payout wallet claim file

## License

MIT — see [LICENSE](LICENSE).
